meta.purpose: How a condition is NAMED to the reader, by the kind of evidence behind it. Wording only: no weight, threshold, score or Disease Master row is read from here.
hierarchy: Direct finding - one measured result against its range (named by the result itself).
Pattern - results that match a defined cluster (named by the cluster).
Risk signal - a pattern that is a recognised RISK FACTOR for a condition; not evidence that the condition is present.
Disease hypothesis - a marker of the disease PROCESS itself; still not a diagnosis.
Confirmed disease - never produced by this system.
meta.rule: A cohort-to-condition link may carry `presented_as`, naming an entry below. A condition is presented under the entry of its largest contribution; a link without `presented_as` keeps the Disease Master name.

cardiovascular_risk_signal.label: Cardiovascular risk signal
cardiovascular_risk_signal.note: These results match a recognised risk factor for coronary artery disease. They are not evidence that the disease is present, which needs clinical assessment and tests such as ECG or imaging.

possible_myocardial_injury.label: Possible acute myocardial injury
possible_myocardial_injury.note: A raised troponin indicates injury to heart muscle. That has several causes - coronary artery disease is one - so it does not by itself establish that disease.
